page.lead: Google Ads and Meta can bring enquiries on day one, unlike SEO where results take months. There is one condition: it has to be visible what comes back. Without tracking wired up properly the budget goes out blind and automated bidding has nothing to learn from.
process: Measurement first, campaigns second. Running ads without conversion tracking means paying for data nobody collects.
A look at competitors: what they bid on, what they promise and roughly what it costs.
A budget calculated from click prices and real conversion rates rather than guessed.
Accounts, campaigns and creatives, including Merchant Center for shops.
Links to GA4, Search Console and the site, so conversions feed back into the system.
Optimisation once data accumulates, then scaling what works.
cases: A campaign running without conversion tracking — Google has nothing to optimise towards and spends on the cheapest clicks.
Broad match with no negatives: paying for queries unrelated to the business.
Ads pointing at the home page instead of the page about that specific service.
One budget covering brand and non-brand queries — brand eats most of it and it looks like success.
No Consent Mode, so a share of conversions is never counted and the campaign looks unprofitable.
page.geo_title: The Slovak market has its own prices
page.geo: Click prices, competition and buyer behaviour in Slovakia differ from larger markets. A budget copied from a foreign guide does not work here. I have worked here for over ten years and know what a click costs in your field and whether ads make sense at all — and if they do not, I say so before you spend.

faq.q: What does campaign setup cost?
faq.a: The hourly rate is 25 EUR and a full launch starts around 1,000 EUR. Ad spend is separate and paid directly to Google or Meta.

faq.q: What budget do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the field and click prices. I calculate it from real figures for your market and name the minimum below which launching is pointless.

faq.q: When will I see results?
faq.a: First enquiries can arrive on launch day, but a meaningful read needs two to four weeks of data.

faq.q: Why insist on tracking before launch?
faq.a: Because without it nobody knows which clicks brought money, and automated bidding has nothing to learn from. It is the most expensive saving in online marketing.

faq.q: Do you manage campaigns ongoing?
faq.a: Yes. After launch continuous optimisation matters — without it a campaign loses performance over time.

page.lead: Most companies run analytics that counts visits but cannot say how many enquiries the site produced. That is not a detail: without proper measurement decisions are guesswork and ad spend is optimised blind. I set up GA4, Tag Manager and conversion tracking so the numbers match reality.
process: An audit of what you have. Very often events turn out to go nowhere, or to be counted twice.
Google Tag Manager and GA4 with Consent Mode v2, so measurement survives the cookie banner.
The events that matter: form submissions, phone, email and WhatsApp clicks, checkout starts.
Marking key events, so enquiries appear as conversions rather than sitting in a list.
Links to Google Ads and Search Console, so it is visible what brings money.
Microsoft Clarity for recordings and heatmaps, where numbers are not enough.
cases: Events pushed to the dataLayer with no GA4 tag in the container to forward them — enquiries are not measured at all.
GA4 loaded twice, once directly and once through Tag Manager, doubling every page view.
A form firing a 'purchase' event with a value when nobody paid, putting revenue that never existed into the reports.
A key event left unmarked, so conversions read zero while enquiries keep arriving.
A cookie banner blocking measurement where it need not, quietly losing data.
page.geo: Analytics in Slovakia is not purely technical. Without consent wired up per Consent Mode v2 you lose data and Google restricts remarketing — and the consent itself has to take the form European rules require. I set up both at once, so neither is sacrificed for the other.

faq.q: What does an analytics setup cost?
faq.a: The hourly rate is 25 EUR, and a full setup for an ordinary company site starts around 500 EUR. I quote after a short audit of what you already have.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Two to five working days for an ordinary site including testing. Longer for a shop with purchase tracking.

faq.q: How will I know measurement actually works?
faq.a: I show you the events arriving in the real-time report and we go through what each one means.

faq.q: Do I need server-side tracking?
faq.a: Not everyone does. It pays off for larger shops and where ad blockers eat a meaningful share of the data. I will tell you honestly whether it is worth it for you.

faq.q: Will I lose historical data?
faq.a: No. The setup does not change what has already been collected, only what is collected from now on.

cookies.seo_keywords: cookie banner, consent mode v2, gdpr slovakia, cookie setup, google consent mode

page.lead: If your site runs analytics or advertising, cookie consent is mandatory — and not just any consent. Since March 2024 Google requires Consent Mode v2; without it you lose data and remarketing is restricted. I build a custom banner that meets the rules and carries no monthly subscription.
process: A banner in your site's own style, not a third-party module bolted on top.
Consent Mode v2 wired correctly into Google Analytics, Tag Manager and the ad accounts.
Consent split into analytics, advertising and functional — not one 'accept everything' button.
The visitor's choice stored, and changeable at any time.
Testing across more than fifteen scenarios: accept, reject, partial consent, repeat visit.
A cookie policy page written to match.
cases: Ready-made tools charge a monthly subscription forever; a custom banner is a one-off.
Most plugins block measurement more than they need to, losing data even where consent was given.
A third-party module slows the site down, which Google reflects in rankings.
With a ready-made tool you do not control what fires when — and that is exactly what decides whether Consent Mode works.
The design cannot be matched to the site without paying extra.
page.geo: The duty to ask for consent does not come from Slovak law but from European rules — GDPR and the ePrivacy directive. Slovakia adopts them, but they are read the same way across the Union. In practice consent must be freely given, specific and revocable, and measurement may only start afterwards. I set it up so you meet the rules and do not lose data needlessly.

faq.q: What does a cookie banner cost?
faq.a: From 200 EUR, one-off. No monthly subscription.

faq.q: Do I need one if I only run Google Analytics?
faq.a: Yes. Analytics cookies require consent too. Only strictly necessary technical cookies are exempt.

faq.q: What happens without one?
faq.a: You risk a fine from the supervisory authority, and Google restricts remarketing while a share of conversions goes uncounted.

faq.q: Will it ruin my statistics?
faq.a: Some data is naturally lost on refusal, but Consent Mode v2 allows modelling to fill the gap. A badly configured banner loses far more.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually two to three working days including testing.

audit.seo_desc: A free SEO audit: technical checks, speed, Google indexing and the errors keeping your site from bringing in customers. Delivered within 3 working days.
audit.h1: Free SEO audit of your website
audit.lead: I go through your site the way Google sees it and tell you exactly what stops it bringing you customers. No fee, no obligation.
audit.why_text: Because it is the most honest way to start. Most sites carry two or three technical faults that quietly take most of the traffic, and until you see them there is no point discussing the price of anything else. Fix them yourself and I am glad. Don't, and at least you know exactly what you are buying.
check_points: Technical foundation: status codes, redirects, www and non-www versions, HTTP against HTTPS — the faults that can make a site invisible to Google.
Indexing: how many pages are actually in Google, which are missing and why. Sitemap, robots.txt, canonical, hreflang.
Speed and Core Web Vitals on mobile and desktop, with the actual causes rather than just a score.
Content and queries: what the site shows up for today, at which positions, and what it needs to reach the first page.
Structured data and how the site looks in search results.
Measurement: whether Google Analytics and Tag Manager actually record enquiries or only page views. This is the most common surprise.
Competitors: who holds your queries in Slovakia and what they have that you don't.
get_points: Findings ordered by impact rather than alphabetically — from what costs you most down to the details.
For each finding, what to do about it and how much work it really is.
What you can fix yourself and what needs a change in the code.
An estimate of which fixes pay off soonest.
time_points: Send your website address through the form below.
Within 3 working days you get the audit in writing.
If you want, we go through it together — in person in Bratislava or online.
audit.who_text: Companies in Slovakia whose site exists but brings no enquiries. Online shops paying for ads without knowing what comes back. And anyone whose site was built by someone else and who is not sure it was done properly.
audit.trust_text: Kirill Mosin, White Eagles & Co. s.r.o. I have lived in Slovakia for more than 10 years, launched 12+ sites for Slovak companies, and know how buyers and institutions behave here. I invoice with a Slovak company number. We speak Slovak, Russian and English.
